quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Decide first what kind of difference this is: a vowel, or a consonant?
quests.explanation: That was "right": the tongue tip curled back without touching the roof of the mouth. "Light" would have touched the ridge just behind the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth, letting air flow around the sides; British /r/ is made with the tongue tip curled slightly back and not touching anything, often with lips a little rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /l/ press the tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep it away from the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is this about the beginning, the vowel, or the ending? Listen for a long rounded sound or a short one.
quests.explanation: "Port" holds a long, rounded vowel with tight lips. "Pot" is over quickly, with a more open jaw.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is short with the mouth open and lips slightly rounded; /ɔː/ is long, with the tongue raised further at the back and the lips more clearly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔː/ round the lips into a clear circle and let the tongue rise a little at the back. For /ɒ/ open the jaw and round the lips only slightly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two short vowels, same ending. Think bright and thin against dull and low.
quests.explanation: The word was "sunk", whose vowel is dull and made low in the mouth. "Sink" is brighter, with the tongue high and forward.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so ignore length and listen to colour instead: bright (/ɪ/) or dull (/ʌ/).
quests.mouthPosition: Lips stay neutral for both, but the jaw is a bit lower for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the first sound, and ask whether the lower lip touches the teeth.
quests.explanation: "Vet" starts with the lip touching the teeth and a buzz. "Wet" starts with rounded lips and no contact.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /w/ uses both lips rounded with no contact between lip and teeth; /v/ uses the lower lip against the upper teeth with friction and a buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: For /v/ bite the lower lip lightly with the upper teeth and vibrate. For /w/ round the lips and do not touch the teeth at all.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is identical in both words. So where is the difference?
quests.explanation: It was "mat": the vowel was quick, and the tongue tip closed sharply. "Mad" stretches the vowel and ends softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The consonants match. Does the vowel move or stay still?
quests.explanation: "Mail" glides upward during the vowel. "Meal" holds one long, high, smiling shape.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ is a diphthong that glides upward and ends with a spread /ɪ/; /iː/ is a steady high vowel. Listen for movement versus stillness.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ start with the jaw half open and close it toward the end. For /iː/ hold a wide smile with the jaw nearly closed.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long. How wide does your jaw need to be?
quests.explanation: "Heart" opens the jaw wide and puts the tongue low. "Hurt" stays half-open with the tongue in the centre.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is long, central and mid-height; /ɑː/ is long, low and back, made with the jaw wide open. Both are long, so listen to how open the mouth is.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɜː/ keep the jaw half open and the lips unrounded. For /ɑː/ drop the jaw fully and pull the tongue low and back.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel, same ending. Listen to what follows the first burst.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "talk", where the tongue tip released with a clean burst. "Chalk" adds a hushing sound right after it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ has a stop followed by hushing friction; /t/ is a clean stop that ends at the release. The extra friction is the cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge. For /t/ release cleanly. For /tʃ/ pull the tongue slightly back and let the air hush out.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both short. Are the lips rounded in the vowel?
quests.explanation: "Luck" leaves the lips relaxed and the vowel flat. "Look" rounds them slightly and sounds deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ has rounded lips and a tongue pulled back and up; /ʌ/ has neutral lips and a central tongue. Lip rounding is the dependable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʊ/ round the lips softly and lift the back of the tongue. For /ʌ/ leave the lips relaxed and open the jaw a little more.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The start and end are the same. What does the vowel do at the end?
quests.explanation: You heard "find", where the vowel finishes spread and bright. "Found" ends with rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /aɪ/ and /aʊ/ both start with an open mouth, but /aɪ/ glides up to a spread /ɪ/ while /aʊ/ glides up and back with lips rounding to /ʊ/. The ending sound is what matters.
quests.mouthPosition: Open the jaw for both. For /aɪ/ finish with the lips spread; for /aʊ/ finish with the lips rounding forward.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the beginning: does the air stop, or keep flowing?
quests.explanation: "Tin" begins with a short burst as the tongue tip is released. "Thin" begins with soft, continuous air between tongue and teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is a fricative with continuous airflow; /t/ is a stop with a complete closure and a burst. Listen for sustained friction versus a sudden release.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ rest the tongue tip against the teeth and let air flow. For /t/ press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth, stop the air, then release.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Pay attention to how long the vowel lasts.
quests.explanation: The word was "pill": a short, loose vowel that reaches the /l/ quickly. "Peel" holds a tense vowel first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are front and high, but /ɪ/ sits slightly lower and more relaxed. The sound your ear catches first is the difference in length: /iː/ lasts noticeably longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Try saying /iː/ with a wide, tense smile, then relax the cheeks and shorten the sound; that slack, quick version is /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel slide, or stay put?
quests.explanation: "Cloak" starts relaxed and closes into a round shape. "Clock" is short and steady.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is a short, steady back vowel; /əʊ/ starts in the centre and glides toward a rounded /ʊ/, so it is longer and moving. One holds still, the other travels.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɒ/ open the jaw, round slightly and stop. For /əʊ/ start with relaxed lips and gradually round them into a small circle as you say it.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are the same after the first sound. Sharp hiss or soft hush?
quests.explanation: It was "said", where the tongue tip stayed near the teeth and the hiss was sharp. "Shed" has a broader hush and rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a broader, lower-pitched hush made with the tongue pulled slightly back and the lips a little rounded; /s/ is a sharper, higher hiss with the tongue tip near the teeth and the lips spread.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ round the lips slightly and pull the tongue back so the air flows over a wider channel. For /s/ spread the lips and bring the tongue tip close to the ridge behind your teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Consider the first sound only. Voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: "Jeep" begins with a buzzing /dʒ/. "Cheap" begins with a breathier, voiceless /tʃ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ share the same tongue movement; /tʃ/ is voiceless and /dʒ/ is voiced. The voiced version has a buzz and a longer preceding vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the tongue against the ridge behind the teeth and release into a hush. Keep the throat silent for /tʃ/; add voice for /dʒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: How wide does the mouth open at the start of the vowel?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "type", where the jaw opened wide first and then closed. "Tape" starts half open and glides a shorter way.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides from a mid-front position up toward /ɪ/, while /aɪ/ starts with a wide-open mouth and glides up. The starting point differs: half-open for /eɪ/, fully open for /aɪ/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /aɪ/ open the jaw wide first, then close it. For /eɪ/ begin half open and close a short distance.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long and open, or short and bright?
quests.explanation: "Park" is longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue back. "Pack" is short and bright.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is short and front with the jaw low; /ɑː/ is long and back with the jaw wide open. Both are open vowels, so listen to duration and front-versus-back colour.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ spread the mouth a little and keep the tongue forward. For /ɑː/ open wide with the tongue low and back, like a yawn.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen at the start: burst of the lips, or buzzing friction?
quests.explanation: "Vote" starts with the lower lip against the teeth and a buzz. "Boat" starts with a pop from the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /b/ is a stop made by closing the lips fully, with a burst; /v/ is a fricative made with lip and teeth, with continuous buzzing airflow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /b/ press both lips together and release. For /v/ touch the lower lip to the upper teeth and let voiced air flow through.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. How does the word end?
quests.explanation: That was "sin", ending with the tongue tip on the ridge. "Sing" would end deeper, with the back of the tongue raised.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /n/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth; /ŋ/ is made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate. Air goes through the nose for both.
quests.mouthPosition: For /n/ press the tongue tip behind the teeth. For /ŋ/ lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate and keep the tip down.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both long. Are the lips rounded or loose?
quests.explanation: "Short" has rounded lips and a darker vowel. "Shirt" leaves the lips loose and the vowel neutral.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is a long central vowel with unrounded lips; /ɔː/ is a long back vowel with clearly rounded lips. Same length, different lip shape and tongue position.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɜː/ keep the lips loose and the tongue in the centre of the mouth. For /ɔː/ round the lips into a circle and pull the tongue back.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Do you hear a slide in the vowel?
quests.explanation: You heard "cost", a short, steady vowel with slightly rounded lips. "Coast" begins open and closes into a round.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a glide: /əʊ/ ends with the lips closing into an 'oo', while /ɒ/ finishes at once.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips tighten during /əʊ/; during /ɒ/ they stay in one position.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The start of the vowel is different. Round or open?
quests.explanation: "Tie" begins with an open, neutral mouth. "Toy" begins with the lips rounded and the tongue back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔɪ/ starts with rounded lips and a back tongue, while /aɪ/ starts with an open, unrounded mouth. Both end in /ɪ/, so listen to the beginning.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔɪ/ start with clearly rounded lips, then spread them as you glide up. For /aɪ/ begin with the jaw open and the lips neutral.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first sound is either smooth or abrupt.
quests.explanation: It was "jet": a stop followed by friction at the start. "Yet" glides in with no stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /j/ is a smooth glide with the tongue rising toward the hard palate; /dʒ/ starts with a stop and ends with friction. The glide is gentle; the affricate is abrupt.
quests.mouthPosition: For /j/ raise the tongue toward the roof of the mouth without touching it. For /dʒ/ press the tongue against the ridge, then release into friction.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for how wide the vowel is before the /nd/.
quests.explanation: "Land" opens the jaw wide and sounds fuller. "Lend" stays at half open and sounds crisper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are front vowels, but /æ/ is lower. That extra openness makes /æ/ sound wider and slightly longer than the crisp, short /e/.
quests.mouthPosition: Place a finger under your chin: the jaw should drop noticeably more for /æ/ than for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both start with a quiet friction. What touches what?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "three", whose friction comes from the tongue tip between the teeth. In "free" it comes from the lip against the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ uses the tongue at the teeth; /f/ uses the lower lip against the upper teeth. Both are quiet, voiceless fricatives, so the difference is subtle; /f/ has slightly stronger friction and /θ/ is softer.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ put the tongue tip lightly between the teeth. For /f/ bring the lower lip up to the upper teeth and keep the tongue out of the way.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short vowels. Rounded lips, or neutral?
quests.explanation: "Dock" has slightly rounded lips and a deeper vowel. "Duck" has neutral lips and a flatter sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is a back vowel with slight lip rounding; /ʌ/ is a central vowel with neutral lips. /ɒ/ sounds rounder and deeper, /ʌ/ sounds flatter and more central.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɒ/ round the lips lightly and pull the tongue back. For /ʌ/ keep the lips neutral and let the tongue lie in the centre.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel steady or gliding?
quests.explanation: "Ball" keeps a steady, rounded, open-mid vowel. "Bowl" begins neutral and closes into a round shape.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔː/ is a long, steady rounded vowel; /əʊ/ begins unrounded in the centre and glides to /ʊ/. Steady and rounded from the start versus a moving sound that rounds late.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔː/ round the lips from the start and keep them there. For /əʊ/ begin with relaxed lips and gradually round them.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both share the long vowel. How does the last hum close?
quests.explanation: That was "teen": the hum finished with the tongue tip on the ridge. "Team" would finish with the lips closing.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /m/ finishes with the lips closed; /n/ finishes with the tongue tip on the ridge and the lips open. The preceding vowel also glides slightly differently.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ end with closed lips. For /n/ end with the lips open and the tongue tip touching the ridge.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. Listen to the ending: a sharp hiss or a soft, airy one?
quests.explanation: "Pass" ends with a sharp, high hiss. "Path" ends with a softer, airy sound as the tongue rests against the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is made by placing the tongue tip against or between the teeth and blowing air softly; /s/ is made with the tongue behind the teeth and a narrow groove, giving a sharper hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ let the tongue tip touch the edge of the upper teeth and blow gently. For /s/ pull the tongue back behind the teeth and narrow the air channel.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The ending is the same. Does the beginning start with a burst?
quests.explanation: The word was "chair": a burst of the tongue followed by a hush. "Share" is a smooth hush with no burst.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a continuous fricative; /tʃ/ begins with a stop and then releases into friction, so it sounds abrupt at the start. Listen for a sudden beginning versus a smooth flow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ let the air flow steadily over the tongue. For /tʃ/ block the air with the tongue against the ridge, then release into a hush.
